article: Manual minute
stem: After reviewing operating data, a chief compliance officer becomes concerned about a compliance dashboard showing stable completion rates while exceptions continue to rise. What response would BEST demonstrate an effective program?
options: Conclude controls are effective because employees completed their attestations.
Reduce monitoring until regulators identify a formal violation.
Test whether controls work in practice, investigate anomalies, and report exception counts while retaining the existing monitoring and remediation plan.
Test whether controls work in practice, investigate anomalies, and use findings to adjust monitoring and remediation.
explanation: The best choice is to test whether controls work in practice, investigate anomalies, and use findings to adjust monitoring and remediation. This approach focuses on monitoring effectiveness rather than relying on an untested shortcut. The other options either substitute assertions for evidence, postpone assessment, or weaken accountability. Editorial basis: CEP 2025-05, Manual minute, p. 13; verify the precise article passage before using this in a scored mock exam.
